name: Atlantic hurricanes
summary: No Atlantic tropical cyclone active or expected; the quiet 2026 season ends on 30 Nov
state: No Atlantic tropical storm or hurricane was found active or threatening land in the run to 25 Nov, and GDACS listed no Atlantic cyclone at 05:41 UTC on 25 Nov (GDACS). AccuWeather said on 9 Nov that the window for further development had closed and that it considered the 2026 season over, after 10 named storms and one hurricane, Isaias, which made landfall near Destin, Florida, on 9 Oct (AccuWeather). With nothing threatening land within five days and the season ending on 30 Nov, the level stays Normal.
for_you: No tropical threat is expected. Anyone travelling to the Caribbean or US Gulf coast can check the National Hurricane Center and FCDO travel advice for updates.
rubric_hit: Normal: no hurricane active and none threatening land within 5 days

sources.title: AccuWeather — The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is over
GDACS — Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System

why: Atlantic hurricanes hit the US Gulf coast, Caribbean and Central America — and refinery and insurance markets with them.
drivers: Sea-surface temperatures, ENSO, wind shear, season timing (Jun–Nov peak Aug–Oct).
